meta_description:
13K likes, 166 comments - hubermanlab on October 8, 2026: "SUCCESS IS DETERMINED BY HOW PRECISELY YOU MATCH YOUR GENUINE CURIOSITY TO THE WORK THAT YOU DO •

Obviously, here I’m talking about career success (but there are parallels to this in other areas of life). 

Also obvious is that we can’t always do the work that we would like to do most. There are practical considerations. 

But ultimately, if we want to make a living doing what we love most and do our very best work, it’s important we invest time in what we are most interested in seeing in the world and curious about.

This clip excerpt is from me as a guest on the podcast Invest With the Best. 

He asked me: “what is the kindest thing anyone has ever done for you?”

My answer was that Barbara Chapman, who eventually became my PhD advisor, had reminded me that the most important thing is to work on the things we are most curious about. And ignore any internal or external noise about what we should be doing instead.

Barbara and I went onto publish a lot of studies together. It was a ton of work, but we had so much fun doing those projects. In no small part because I was trying to answer the questions about the brain and brain development that were most burning for me at the time. 

Some years later, I shifted to working on other scientific questions (postdoc years) and then again (before tenure) and again (after tenure) and I eventually launched the Huberman Lab podcast. 

Because that’s where my curiosity went. Each stage worked out great. And there will be a next stage of interests at some point too. 

None of it came easy, but I’m so glad Barbara convinced me to follow my curiosity. Always. 

The takeaway is that whether field or career track is crowded or empty, if you follow your strongest curiosity, your motivation never flags (if you take care of yourself physically that is!) and you inevitably do your best work.

So once again, while there are practical considerations along one’s life and career track, when you can, follow your curiosity, even if it means going against the grain. 

I did. And I never looked back. And I’ll continue to do that going forward. 

My wish for everyone - for you, is that you do the same.".
